t: Prague grew from a castle of the Přemyslid rulers into the seat of the kings of Bohemia, and under Charles IV, who was crowned emperor in 1355, it became the capital of the Holy Roman Empire.

The city was the centre of the Hussite movement after the burning of Jan Hus in 1415, and the defenestration of 1618 and the defeat at White Mountain in 1620 began its re-Catholicisation and a long decline.
Prague became the capital of Czechoslovakia in 1918, was occupied by Germany in 1939 and by the Warsaw Pact in 1968, and has been the capital of the Czech Republic since 1993.
dyk: The city's four boroughs of Hradčany, Malá Strana, Staré Město and Nové Město were merged into a single entity in 1784 under Joseph II, and the Jewish quarter of Josefov was added in 1850.
ev: Bořivoj builds Prague Castle and moves his seat there
A bishopric is founded in Bohemia, with the bishop's palace on the castle grounds
Charles IV founds the University of Prague and the New Town
The Prague crowd throws the city's councillors from the New Town Hall, and the Hussite Wars follow
The Protestant army is defeated at the Battle of White Mountain
Joseph II merges the four towns of Prague into a single city
German forces enter Prague, and Bohemia and Moravia become a protectorate
The Velvet Revolution ends communist rule in Czechoslovakia

f.founded: Prague Castle was begun by Bořivoj around 880, on a fortified settlement that had existed on the site since 800; legend attributes the city's founding to the duchess Libuše and her husband Přemysl.
f.where: On the Vltava river in Bohemia, in the Czech Republic, with the castle on the west bank and the fort of Vyšehrad to the south.
f.known: Prague Castle and St Vitus Cathedral; Charles IV's imperial capital; Charles University; Jan Hus and the Hussite Wars; the court of Rudolf II; the defenestrations of Prague; the Jewish quarter; the Prague Spring and the Velvet Revolution
f.today: Prague is the capital and largest city of the Czech Republic, with a population of about 1.4 million.
